bluf: fifty-five is a Paris data company owned by The Brandtech Group, founded in 2010 by former Google executives per its about page, with 300+ people and ten offices across Europe, Greater China, Singapore and New York. It sells the data foundation under marketing: strategy, cloud and AI, mix modelling and measurement, CX. Where it is going: deeper into AI transformation on that foundation, with a Digital Twin MMM and an AI Focus Group as products; the record shows no dated move and no price. The thing a rival should know: all 13 named clients are names only, and its own site publishes nothing the sitemap read could count.
doing:
fifty-five positions itself as a self described data company helping brands build the data foundation that turns AI into a performance engine, across strategy, cloud and AI, media consulting and CX. In plain words: a consultancy that sells data engineering, governance and measurement first and treats media and AI as things that only work once the data is fixed. Its H1 reads The data company. The headline claim is a case index line, saving TotalEnergies €4M and lifting marketing efficiency 20% with an in house MMM, quoted as its claim.

The sold mix has one lead line, data and measurement (scored 3: media mix modelling and performance measurement lines, MMM cases for Estée Lauder and TotalEnergies), with AI automation the second core line (scored 2: data powered AI transformation on the homepage, a Cloud services & AI line that automates operations, an AI focus group case). Everything else is thin: CRO, paid search, paid social and programmatic score 1 each with no evidence note, and SEO, AI search, content, creator, CRM, local, retail media and web build score 0. The service list adds organization and skills, digital due diligence, sustainability, data engineering, data science, data governance, media operation and customer experience. Proprietary products: Digital Twin MMM and an AI Focus Group for brand perception research. No partners are listed.

AI posture: data foundations as the precondition for useful AI, sold as cloud and AI services, data powered AI transformation and AI tools. The moves list is empty and no news, case studies or jobs were captured, so the record holds no dated move. Pricing signals: none. Conspicuously absent for a data company of its kind: any AI search or citation measurement line (AI search scores 0), any retail media or commerce data work (0), and any CRM or owned audience line (0), for a firm whose book is luxury, cosmetics and banking.
clients:
The record types the client as enterprise, in luxury, cosmetics and banking and financial services, with Paris as home and offices in London, Geneva, Milan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Taipei, Singapore and New York; its Google ad advertisers include 55 SAS and Fifty-Five HK Limited, so the buying runs through France and Hong Kong at least.

The needs read lists 13 clients, 0 observed and 13 named only, all from the case studies index page with no work described: Guerlain, Leroy Merlin, Estée Lauder, SPCA Hong Kong, Pierre & Vacances-Center Parcs, Bouygues Telecom, ORPI, Renault Group, Carmila, Chomp, ADEO, Olight and TotalEnergies, so no mix can be computed. The needs are inferred from what the agency leads with: data and measurement, mix modelling first. Two names carry a hint from the capability notes: Estée Lauder and TotalEnergies are cited as MMM cases, and the TotalEnergies line claims €4M saved and 20% efficiency, a data and measurement need observed only as a claim.

Two clients are shared with other tracked agencies: Leroy Merlin also sits on the books of labelium and k2-internet, and Bouygues Telecom on the book of artefact. The whole book is names only (13 of 13), which the record flags as a question to ask its clients.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places fifty-five best for KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better) and KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), both driven by data and measurement, and most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out). It is very likely, with moderate confidence, that these enterprise brands keep buying measurement and MMM as platform automation removes their media agencies' hours, and likely that they will ask for AI answer measurement, which the record shows fifty-five does not sell.

openings:
The strongest opening is proof. fifty-five sells measurement to enterprise brands and its record describes no engagement: 13 of 13 clients are names on an index page, the only figures are a TotalEnergies claim of €4M and 20%, and its own site publishes nothing the sitemap read could count. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival with described MMM and measurement cases can take a luxury or cosmetics account (Guerlain, Estée Lauder) in a procurement that asks for method. Falsifier: fifty-five publishing case pages that describe the model, the data and the result for named clients.

Second, no public pricing model, so an outcome priced measurement offer is a conversation it cannot hold in public. Third, the shoppers: Leroy Merlin already buys from labelium and k2-internet, and Bouygues Telecom from artefact, so both are a roughly even chance to be contestable on measurement. Fourth, the KJ6 exposure: the hollowing removes consulting hours in data strategy and organization work, and AI operator delivery of the same undercuts it, though the Monsoon Breeze band (44.5) and displacement of 37.0 say this book does not buy on price: lead with method and AI answer measurement, which it does not sell.
